headline: P0161 (Family Practice, GA): 99215 share of 30.8% vs 3.2% expected; elevated even on patients with 0-1 chronic conditions, a pattern consistent with upcoding
rationale: P0161 billed 77 of 250 claims (30.8%) as 99215. The expected share given its patients' complexity is about 3.2% (z vs peers 3.89, risk-adjusted score 9.0). The excess is not limited to sicker patients. Among patients with 0 chronic conditions, 12 of 44 visits (27.3%) were billed as 99215, against 2.1% for all providers. Among patients with 1 condition, 28 of 97 visits (28.9%) were 99215, against 3.4%. Together these two groups account for 40 of the 77 99215s. The sampled low-complexity 99215 claims mostly carry single, routine-looking diagnoses: rash R21 (C0073067, C0073103), UTI N39.0 (C0073101, C0073108, C0073165, C0073175, C0073263), unspecified abdominal pain R10.9 (C0073075), follow-up Z09 (C0073162) and uncomplicated hypertension I10 (C0073100, C0073241). On their face these would not usually support high-complexity medical decision-making. Some of the 4+ condition 99215s look plausible (C0073082, C0073236), but those groups are small (18 visits), and the same patients are also billed at lower levels (C0073070 is a 99213 for patient N0024; C0073237 is a 99214 for N0018). No clinical documentation, time records or MDM notes are in the packet, so these findings are claims-level only and the sample lists are not exhaustive.
next_steps: Request medical records for the sampled 99215 claims on 0-1 condition patients (e.g., C0073067, C0073108, C0073162, C0073075) and check whether MDM or total time supports level 5 under the 2021 E/M guidelines.
Check whether time-based billing is being used and whether documented time is plausible against daily visit volume.
Pull the provider's full claim set, not just the samples, to confirm the 99215 distribution by diagnosis, especially acute minor diagnoses (N39.0, R21, J06.9, Z09).
Compare the same patients across visits (e.g., N0024, N0018, N0012) to see whether level selection follows clinical changes or is applied inconsistently.
Look for EHR templating, cloned notes or default level-5 selections, and check whether the 99215 rate is stable over 2024 or rose sharply.
